utterances.text: Yes. I have also mentioned the rifts among the Serbs. And it also applies to other peoples. This is probably inherent to the Balkans. In our region, there was a division into the supporters of Fikret Abdic and the supporters of the SDA hard-liners, whose leader was Alija Izetbegovic. We co-operated with those who supported Fikret Abdic and wanted peace in the region. They wanted many things to be tackled differently. But we also took every opportunity to maintain good relations with Bihac, which was the -- the spearhead of the SDA hard-liners. We wanted to avoid shooting and the destruction of property because we knew we didn't play an important role in the resolution of the global situation. We only wanted there to be as few victims as possible and as little suffering because we knew that only in such a way would we be able to build a sound Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When the war broke out, did have you information about convoys passing through and did you have information about the misuse of convoys for the arming of the 5th Corps?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO KLICKOVIC
utterances.text: This is a rather broad question. I need a couple of sentences to answer it. But there are also -- there's also more than one segment to it. Let me point out that the -- that international aid that came to the Cazin region, which is near Bihac, we have information, including documents, that instead of fuel and food, ammunition and weapons were -- were being transported. And this Tribunal saw these documents in other trials. I will single out two persons who were involved. Hajrudin Osmanagic, commander of the District Staff of Bihac, and Sead Palic, an intelligence guy from Bosanska Krupa. He was born at Ostraznica [phoen] and he worked for that humanitarian aid organisation, but when we found his documents we saw what was being transported, from sniper-sights, through ammunition, through barrels for light weapons. In other words, lethal assets. That's not all. There was the Corolici [phoen] airstrip that you could access by helicopter or by smaller transport planes. It was used for the transportation of provisions for the 5th Corps. And let me also say that JNA units also passed through the area. Often individuals or small groups of soldiers or officers were stopped and robbed of their weapons, ammunition, or means of transport. We have specific evidence to corroborate that because the Secretariat of the Interior at Bosanska Krupa, their crime investigation service, staffed by Serbs, initiated about a dozen proceedings against persons who committed crimes of alienation of property and so on. However, the proceedings were never completed, and it is clear why. Because it was the policy of SDA that decided about everything, including who would be tried and who would not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. 1D8890. Could we please see it. I will show you only one document, Mr. Klickovic. I will tender the rest over -- over the bar table.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. At this point, I'd like to note that we've had nearly an hour of detailed direct examination, much of which going well beyond the scope of the witness's statement. I'd like to note that we had no advance notice that this would take place, no information by way of a proofing note or anything else that the -- this information be elicited. No notice that this document would be used in the direct examination. Obviously this makes our cross-examination preparations -- hampers our cross-examination preparations and our estimates, and this is the kind of notice that we're entitled under Rule 65 ter, and I'd just like to ask that, in the future, this not happened again, that we get the notice to which we're entitled. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Fair enough.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I assume responsibility for that. It's very true. But this statement has really been butchered. And I wanted to point out this municipality as an example for leading Defence evidence. Since that has all been cut out, I must now ask general questions to elicit the information desired. If he was merely a municipal dignitary, he was also a member of government, and so on. And I really apologise for these documents. There is more than one. But I'll show only one so that Mr. Klickovic can comment on it. Could you please zoom in.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you, Mr. Klickovic, tell us what this document is. Who is sending it to who?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO KLICKOVIC
utterances.text: Even without looking at it, not only this one but a series of such documents, they were considered by the court in Bosnia-Herzegovina where I was tried. I know very well what it says. This clearly shows what kind of aid was being provided and to who. We know who, at the time, was commander of the 5th Corps of the BH army, Ramiz Drekovic. We know through who that went to Bihac. As I said, Sead Palic was in charge of Krupa.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Klickovic, since we do not have English translation, we do not know what this is about. So please tell us what this document is about and then proceed to explain whatever you like.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I apologise. This document is about ammunition supplies for the 5th Corps and the supply of explosive devices that the 5th Corps used for combat purposes. This document is marked military secret, strictly confidential, and this was a job that was done by people that I mentioned: Hajrudin Osmanagic, Commander of staff, and his deputy, Hadzic. At that time, they did about their work in Zagreb. They had something similar to an embassy, or maybe it was an embassy department, and it was all sent to the commander of the 5th Corps, Ramiz Drekovic -- or, rather, his command. I doubt that he as commander actually counted bullets. So this document shows what was being transported instead of humanitarian aid. We also had information who manned in -- border crossings at the time of the -- of the international forces up there. Whether they controlled what was in the tank or trunks or not, we don't know. But we know that under the veil of humanitarian aid, something else was being transported. We tolerated that because we let humanitarian aid pass through our territory, even if it was for the Muslims or the Croats. It was pursuant to the orders of Dr. Karadzic. This was not the first time that, instead of food and medication, ammunition, explosive devices, rocket fuel were being transported. I was shown a number of such documents, and I personally made it part of defence evidence at the BH Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And could you please tell us through who did this happen. Who transported these assets?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO KLICKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know if I confirmed that already, but all of this was done with the agreement of the UNHCR and the international sponsors, meaning that those assets that were being transported did not have to be their property but they had their markings and were under their control and monitoring. These were assets, transport means that would cross over exclusively under the supervision of international factors.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I would like to tender this document, please, and I have no further questions at this point for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It receives MFI D4314, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I take it you can start your cross-examination, Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And good afternoon, Mr. Klickovic.

utterances.speaker: GOJKO KLICKOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: If I could just start by clarifying the dates -- periods during which you served as prime minister. Is it correct that you were the prime minister of the Republika Srpska between roughly May 1996 and January 1998?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO KLICKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: At -- in your statement, you talk about the Variant A and B document, and you spoke about it at length as well this afternoon. You claim that the document had no binding character and, indeed, today you said "it meant nothing to me." You did, in Bosanska Krupa, create a Crisis Staff pursuant to the Variant A and B instructions, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO KLICKOVIC
utterances.text: No. We formed a Crisis Staff pursuant to the Law on All People's Defence of the Socialist of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Articles 98, 99, 100, 101, 102, 103 and 104.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: If we could have 65 ter 06700, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Transcript, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ah, it's all right now. I see that it has been corrected now. That it's all right now. 100. 102. I think 102 is missing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: You can see, Mr. Klickovic, this is an extract from the minutes of the 3rd Session of the Bosanska Krupa Serb Municipal Assembly Executive Committee held on 24 December 1991 with you chairing and conducting the proceedings. And you can see the agenda item 3(a) is implementing the instruction on establishing a Crisis Staff; and on the next page, in the B/C/S, at the bottom of the page in the English, under item 3(a) it says: "The chairman briefed those present on the instruction on establishing SDS Crisis Staffs in BH, and, in accordance with the said instruction, proposed the establishment of a Crisis Staff. This was followed by establishment of the Crisis Staff of the following makeup..." And then it lists the members. Now, the instruction on establishing SDS Crisis Staffs in BH that you referred to in this meeting is the Variant A and B instructions ; correct?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO KLICKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct that it says so in the minutes. But I was obliged to inform everybody with any document that arrived. However, the Crisis Staffs are a legal category, and there is no dilemma about that. The War Presidencies are constitutional category. And I did say what the basis was for this to our members. Membership in the Crisis Staff is regulated by law, by Article 67 of the Law on All People's Defence, which states precisely who would become a member of the Crisis Staff. By virtue of their function here, they're just mentioned by their names: Deputy, chairman, and so on. Only names are added, but everything is regulated by laws, and there's no need for any other papers or any instructions. Everything is already there. I think the deputy brought it, and I was obliged to inform everybody that this instruction exists, and that this will be something that will be done in all our neighbouring municipalities, and we, ourselves, also had our own municipality and our own, organs and we would implement it there.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And the document says: "And in accordance with the said instruction," which you've agreed is the Variant A and B instruction, you proposed the establishment of a Crisis Staff. This was followed by establishment of the Crisis Staff. Now that reflects the municipal leadership, SDS leadership establishing a Crisis Staff in Bosanska Krupa pursuant to the Variant A and B instructions; correct?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO KLICKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't see anywhere that it says Variant A and B. Therefore, there is no Variant A and B. The regulations regulated the forming of the Crisis Staffs. We just used the document that arrived for information purposes only. We would have done this without it as well because it's not binding. Secondly, at the time the situation in our area became critical. Had we needed it, we would have formed the Crisis Staff even earlier, but we believed that we would overcome the situation in talks with our partners in the SDA and that we would not be needing a Crisis Staff at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I tender this document. And I'd like 65 ter 26007, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll receive it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It receives exhibit number P6661, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And if we could have page 30 of the English and page 27 of the B/C/S of this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Klickovic, the document coming up now is a part of the interview you gave to the Office of the Prosecution in 2003. And I'd like to direct your attention to the bottom of your page in your language. It's the middle of the page in the English. Where you are asked about the very document we just saw, which has the reference number 0091-4271. And you're asked: "You are familiar with this document? Do you remember it?" And you say: "I remember the content of the document and that, so that's the -- you know, the least problem. I remember the content because it was the result of the instructions." And then the investigator describes the document and says: "It states that the Crisis Staff is actually being set up. Do you agree with that?" And you answer: "Yes." Now, again, your reference here to the instructions is a reference to the Variant A and B instructions; correct?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO KLICKOVIC
utterances.text: Again, in this statement also - which was given a long time ago - the Variant A and B document is not mentioned. The law does not recognise Variant A and B, and that is why I never mentioned Variant A and B. I simply spoke about the instruction before the investigative organs because I was forced to do so because they did not even want to hear that there were constitutional and legal regulations on this matter. I tried to explain how the instruction came about. However, no one was interested. I said in the beginning that the instruction is a very strange document and that somebody misused it to substantial degree.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: If we could go to the next page in both languages. You said no one was interested in hearing your reasons about the creation of the Crisis Staff. On this page, at the top in the English, and in the middle in the B/C/S, you were asked: "Right. And the reason for that creation of this Crisis Staff was what?" And you said: "The situation at the time in the area, the instructions that came from the SDS party, and also the results of the events of events that went on in the second paragraph of October." You refer to the plebiscite, the memorandum on independence. And then you say: "So those -- all those events resulted in these instructions. Both -- they came from both the president of the party and the executive body of the party." Now, here, Mr. Klickovic, you were asked directly why the Crisis Staff was created. You do not refer to the Law on All People's Defence in any manner whatsoever. You refer to the instructions that came from the president and the executive body of the party, and that is a reference to the Variant A and B instructions, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO KLICKOVIC
utterances.text: Again, I do not refer to Variant A and B. And, secondly, I said that reference to any kind of rule or law before any prosecutor's office meant nothing. They kept going back to instructions, Variant A and B. It's correct that I said that the Crisis Staff was formed because of the situation in the field and because of the instructions that came from the top, in order to prevent an escalation of the conflict because of certain minor things and other things that were happening. Because I said that it was these instructions that were a limiting factor in terms of the conflict. And if I remember correctly, I said that here as well to an investigator of The Hague Tribunal, that the situation in the field was such that the time of crisis had already arrived. However, during a crisis, during -- Crisis Staffs are formed pursuant to the relevant laws.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... we saw a moment ago that you created a Crisis Staff in Bosanska Krupa on the 24th of December, 1991. That is, four days after the Variant A and B instructions were issued. We see here in your previous interview that you said the Crisis Staff was created pursuant to instructions that came from the president and the executive body of the party. If you are not talking about the Variant A and B instructions, what are -- instructions are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: GOJKO KLICKOVIC
utterances.text: I did not talk about Variant A and B. I do not intend to talk about them, and I'm not interested about them. I'm talking about the legal organ, which is based on key legal organs in force at the time. The Crisis Staff is an institution which, during times of crisis, has the task of restoring the original situation, or resolving a situation, if the situation begins to escalate out of control. Why are we talking about the 24th? I could have formed the Crisis Staff on the 19th in the evening. I could have done it as soon as I arrived. However, there are activities of the Crisis Staff in Bosanska Krupa before the 19th. We need to find the date on when the order of evacuation was issued, or the order on the transfer of endangered Serb citizens from the left to the right bank. And then you will see that without a Crisis Staff being named, it was actually doing its work. So this cannot be connected in any way to the paper that I received from the party because, as I said, even today, that paper means nothing to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I tender these two pages of the interview.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It receives exhibit number P6662, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot find in the Serbian version what the Prosecutor said about something coming from the president. There is no coming from the president in the Serbian version. Perhaps we can look at the document again, both in Serbian and in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I see in the middle -- at line 20... my B/C/S is basically non-existent. But there appears to be a line -- a reference to the president of the SDS in line 21 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please ask the original to be read so that the interpreter could translate it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Yes, Mr. Klickovic. Could you read out your words there so that we can hear the translation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mean "GK, 16? The current situation," is that what I'm supposed to read?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "The current situation in that area and the instructions that came from the Serbian Democratic Party as a consequence of events from the second half of October, the plebiscite of the Serbian people, as a reaction to the declaration of independence or, rather, the initiative to the memorandum..." The initiative of the memorandum had not been clarified yet. And then: "Following that course of events," this activity came, meaning "instructions from the party level and representatives of the SDS in executive organs of the joint power."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In line 11, "predstavnik," "representative," was turned into "predsjednik," "president."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: If I could just clarify -- this is the usual situation with interviews where it is not a translation but it's two transcriptions of what is happening simultaneously in two languages, so sometimes the transcripts aren't verbatim. I note the time, if Your Honours wish to break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll adjourn for today and resume tomorrow at 9.00. Mr. Klickovic, I'd like to advise you not to discuss about your testimony with anybody else while you are giving testimony here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 12th day of February, 2014, at 9.00 a.m.
